examples.question_text:
Find the missing fraction.
(a) Multiplying a fraction by $\frac49$ gives $\frac7{15}$.
(b) Dividing a fraction by $\frac7{10}$ gives $\frac38$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Undo multiplying by $\frac49$ by dividing by it.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac7{15}\div\frac49\\&=\frac7{15}\times\frac94\\&=\frac{63}{60}\\&=\frac{21}{20}\end{aligned}$
Check: $\frac{21}{20}\times\frac49=\frac7{15}$.

(b) Undo dividing by $\frac7{10}$ by multiplying by it.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac38\times\frac7{10}\\&=\frac{21}{80}\end{aligned}$
Check: $\frac{21}{80}\div\frac7{10}=\frac38$.

(a) Write the whole number as a fraction over $1$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac35\times4\\&=\frac35\times\frac41\\&=\frac{12}{5}\\&=2\frac25\end{aligned}$

(b) The word 'of' means multiply.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac34\times\frac27\\&=\frac{3\times2}{4\times7}\\&=\frac6{28}\\&=\frac3{14}\end{aligned}$

(c) Write $4$ as $\frac41$, then multiply by its reciprocal.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac7{10}\div4\\&=\frac7{10}\div\frac41\\&=\frac7{10}\times\frac14\\&=\frac7{40}\end{aligned}$

Convert both mixed numbers to improper fractions, then multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\frac14\div1\frac35\\&=\frac94\div\frac85\\&=\frac94\times\frac58\\&=\frac{45}{32}\\&=1\frac{13}{32}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: 3/8 × 7/11 = 21/88. The mixed numbers convert to 30/7 and 11/8; their product is 330/56 = 165/28 = 5 25/28. Methods match source lines 2384–2398 and 2679–2696. Formatting preserves the original mathematics and adds appropriate continuation gutters.

7/9 ÷ 4/11 = 7/9 × 11/4 = 77/36 = 2 5/36. Working left to right, 5/8 ÷ 3/7 = 35/24, then 35/24 × 2/9 = 70/216 = 35/108. Methods match source lines 3425–3431 and 3792–3798. The independent equation correctly has no phantom equals.

The first missing fraction is 7/15 ÷ 4/9 = 63/60 = 21/20; multiplying it by 4/9 gives 7/15. The second is 3/8 × 7/10 = 21/80; dividing it by 7/10 gives 3/8. Missing-factor and missing-dividend tasks are supported by source Q7d (image127) and Q17d–e (image183). Formatting preserves the inverse operations and checks.

3/5 × 4/1 = 12/5 = 2 2/5. Three quarters of 2/7 is 3/4 × 2/7 = 6/28 = 3/14. Finally, 7/10 ÷ 4/1 = 7/10 × 1/4 = 7/40. These use changed values and the methods supplied at lines 2486–2496, 2418 and 3427–3431.

2 1/4 = 9/4 and 1 3/5 = 8/5. Thus 9/4 ÷ 8/5 = 9/4 × 5/8 = 45/32 = 1 13/32. Conversion and reciprocal division match source lines 2679–2684, 3417–3421 and the mixed-number division exercise at 3773–3777.
